manifest.name: Flood-Net
manifest.tagline: The engineering register and toolset for the Bureau's Queensland flood-warning radio network: stations, repeaters, health, field work.
manifest.about: Flood-Net is the register and toolset for the Bureau of Meteorology's Queensland (and neighbouring) flood-warning telemetry network: the field stations, the repeaters that relay them, the base stations and the radio paths between. It is a browser app with no build step, backed by a Supabase Postgres database and a Cloudflare Worker at floodwarning.net, for the people who plan, inspect and keep the network running. It takes readings in from base stations, judges the network's health on a schedule, publishes a daily animated bulletin, and serves public station data to AI agents through a read-only API and MCP server. It is not a flood warning service.

components.name: Agent API and MCP server

provides.name: Agent API (REST and MCP)
provides.what: Read-only public station data: search and stations near a point, a station's record and dossier, readings and the latest reading per station, health findings and silent stations, flood levels, a station's benchmarks in numbers (level, datum, what each reads on the gauge), service levels, ACMA licences, a station's radio path to the base stations with the fade margin saved for each hop, catchments, networks, and a changelog of every visible API change.

provides.name: Benchmarks for SoRT (the hand-back)
provides.what: SoRT's scope builder asks for one station's Bureau benchmarks (0101, editors only) without them ever reaching the public API: it calls window.open('https://floodwarning.net/#benchmarks-for-sort=<base64url of UTF-8 JSON {v:1, source:'sort', nonce [A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}, station:{id, number, name}}>', 'floodnet-sort-bridge'), keeping the opener. Flood-Net reads it as untrusted, clears the fragment and keeps it in the tab's sessionStorage across a sign-in, finds the station by id else by bureau number (bureau_key's rule), and shows a signed-in editor the marks exactly as they will go. Send to SoRT posts {type:'floodnet:benchmarks', v:1, nonce, station:{id, number, name}, printed_on, benchmarks:[{ord, level_m, datum (AHD|STATE|ASSUM|UNKNOWN), on_gauge_m, gauge_zero_m, gauge_datum, description, comment}] in ord order} by window.opener.postMessage to https://cdomotor-g.github.io and no other origin; with no opener, Copy for SoRT puts 'floodnet-benchmarks:' + base64url of the same JSON on the clipboard for SoRT's Paste from Flood-Net box. A non-editor is told only editors can see them and nothing is sent.

provides.name: SoRT's forum sessions (the passphrase store)
provides.what: A small file store for the SoRT scope builder's forum sessions at https://floodwarning.net/api/sort/v1, behind one shared forum passphrase and no accounts: every request but the preflight carries X-SoRT-Passphrase, accepted when sha256_hex('sort-forum-v1:' + passphrase) is the Worker's hash (SORT_PASS_SHA256 if set, else the constant in worker/sort.js), else 401 {error:'passphrase'}. GET /check is 200 {ok:true}; GET /files/<path> the file's text with its ETag, no-store, or 404 {error:'not found'}; PUT /files/<path> the whole file as JSON, at most 4 MB (413 {error:'too large'}, 400 {error:'not JSON'}), with If-None-Match: * to create or If-Match: "<etag>" to replace, else or on a conflict 412 {error:'changed'}, and 200 {etag} with the ETag header. <path> is index.json or stations/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}.json (else 400 {error:'path'}). CORS for https://cdomotor-g.github.io and https://floodwarning.net only (GET, PUT, OPTIONS; content-type, x-sort-passphrase, if-match, if-none-match; ETag exposed). 120 requests and 10 wrong passphrases a minute per address, then 429 {error:'slow down'}. Kept in R2 under _meganet/sort/files/, with each UTC hour's last save copied to _meganet/sort/history/<path>/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH>Z.json. Not part of the agent API.

manifest.about: Turns a Raspberry Pi into an ALERT and ALERT2 base station. Its Node agent finds RTL-SDR sticks, Quansheng ALERT radios, ELPRO ERT-A2 receivers and a GPS by itself, decodes every burst with Flood-Net's own decoders, keeps readings in a queue on disk and posts them to Flood-Net's ingest. It checks in with Flood-Net's Base Stations tab once a minute, so an administrator can see its health, change its settings and update it from there. A set-up page on GitHub Pages picks the image and writes the SD card's settings, for whoever puts a base station on a site.

manifest.name: ALERT_PACKETS
manifest.tagline: A one-page decoder and encoder for ALERT/ERTS packets (ABF, BCC, EAF, EIF), built on the Bureau's ERTS Data Formats spec.
manifest.about: Paste a 40-bit framed message, a 32-bit payload or 8-digit hex and it is decoded against every known format, with check bits and CRC validated and a colour-coded bit map; or encode the other way. Decoded addresses are named from a national ALERT address file, and the page can be driven from the URL with a JSON result. Flood-Net absorbed it: its ALERT Packets tab (packets.js) is the maintained port, carrying the same address file and spec byte for byte.

manifest.tagline: A zero-cost smart-home dashboard: LPUs post sensor readings to ThingSpeak, and a GitHub Pages page charts them against the forecast.
